title: Audit Logging Program Kickoff (internal)
summary: Internal kickoff for the audit logging schema standardization + coverage program. Team aligned on goals (canonical schema v1, shared emit/validate libs, sensitive action inventory, CI enforcement, reliability SLO + export hardening) and agreed to an “inventory first” execution sequence to avoid missing events and rework. Owners and timelines were assigned for schema draft, naming guidelines alignment, initial sensitive action inventory, and first instrumentation targets (API keys, RBAC changes, model rollout actions).
topics: Program goals and definition of “sensitive action”
Phasing and timeline (inventory → schema v1 + libraries → instrumentation → reliability/reporting → beta/GA)
Event schema requirements (actor/target model, correlation IDs, outcome/error semantics, redaction)
Coverage enforcement approach (inventory mapping + CI gate + integration tests)
Reliability requirements (delivery lag SLO, retry semantics, exporter sinks)
Immediate next milestones and workstream owners
action_items: Elliot Price: Create Confluence “Audit logging program overview” draft with timeline, owners, and links; share for review by 2025-05-23.
Mei Lin: Start the sensitive actions inventory sheet (API/Console/Dedicated/Private) with initial owners + coverage status; seed with top 30 actions by 2025-05-24.
Allison Grant: Draft audit event naming guidelines (namespace boundaries: api.*, console.*, rbac.*, deploy.*, dedicated.*, private.*) and circulate for async feedback by 2025-05-22.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Provide the definitive list of auth/RBAC + API key sensitive actions and expected events (create/rotate/revoke, role change diffs) by 2025-05-24.
Amara Diallo: Confirm request_id + actor propagation path through API gateway and flag gaps; propose implementation plan by 2025-05-28.
Nadia Rahman: Outline where schema validation should occur (service vs pipeline) and expected performance overhead; bring recommendation to next sync by 2025-05-27.
Rafael Mendes: Pull baseline delivery lag numbers from current pipeline and propose initial SLO + alerting thresholds by 2025-05-29.
Olga Petrov: Identify SOC 2/ISO evidence expectations specifically for audit logs (fields, retention, access controls) and draft mapping outline by 2025-05-30.
Marcus Lin: Define redaction requirements (no secrets/tokens) and internal access expectations; provide security review checklist by 2025-05-27.
Connor O'Brien: Draft a 2-quarter milestone plan with beta gates and dependencies; post in Linear initiative by 2025-05-24.
next_steps: Publish initial sensitive action inventory and use it to drive instrumentation sequencing (“inventory first”).
Produce schema v1 draft + examples and run a cross-team review (Security, Telemetry, Console, Private).
Pick 2–3 early instrumentation slices for fast wins (API keys, RBAC changes, model rollout actions).
Define delivery lag SLO and the required dashboards/alerts before beta outreach begins.
transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Title: Audit Logging Program Kickoff (internal)
Date: 2025-05-20
Time: 10:05 AM PT
Duration: 53 minutes

Attendees (Redwood Inference): Naomi Feldman, Marcus Lin, Olga Petrov, Nadia Rahman, Rafael Mendes, Kaitlyn Nguyen, Amara Diallo, Mei Lin, Allison Grant, Elliot Price, Connor O'Brien

---
Auto-generated Notes (draft)
Summary:
- Align on objectives: canonical audit event schema v1, shared logging/validation library, full coverage for sensitive actions, reliable pipeline + exports.
- Decision: start with a single sensitive action inventory (“inventory first”), then schema + libs, then instrumentation/migration.

Action items:
- (See Action items section above)

---

[00:00] Naomi Feldman: Alright, hi everyone. Thanks for joining on short notice. This is the kickoff for the audit logging program. The goal today is to get aligned on scope, roles, and the timeline, and then agree on the first two weeks of work.

[00:18] Naomi Feldman: Context: enterprise deals are starting to ask for audit logs as a gating item, and we also have SOC two evidence expectations coming up. We have audit-ish events in a few places but it’s not consistent. We need a canonical schema and, importantly, coverage for sensitive actions.

[00:36] Marcus Lin: Yeah. Plus the current situation is kind of… it’s not just inconsistent, it’s easy to bypass. Like one code path logs, the other doesn’t. That’s exactly what auditors and customers will find.

[00:48] Olga Petrov: And from GRC side, we keep getting questionnaires that ask “do you log admin actions like key rotation, permission changes, retention changes,” and we can’t answer cleanly.

[01:02] Naomi Feldman: Great. So two definitions to anchor: “audit log” here means security-relevant, administrative events that materially impact customer data access, security posture, billing, availability. Not all observability events. We’re not sampling.

[01:20] Allison Grant: Thank you for saying “not sampling.” Just to be explicit: audit logs must be complete by design, so anything like “drop under load” is a hard no.

[01:30] Nadia Rahman: Yep. Also means the pipeline needs backpressure semantics and a clear “delay vs drop” metric.

[01:37] Naomi Feldman: Exactly. Agenda: (1) roles/owners, (2) timeline/phases, (3) decisions today—particularly the sequencing, (4) action items.

[01:50] Connor O'Brien: I’ll capture milestones and translate to Linear after.

[01:54] Naomi Feldman: Cool.

[02:00] Naomi Feldman: Roles: I’m product owner. Marcus is security eng owner. Olga is mapping to SOC/ISO. Nadia is telemetry/pipeline. Rafael is SRE for SLOs and runbooks. Kaitlyn and Amara are the first instrumentation wave on auth/RBAC and gateway. Allison for naming/standards. Mei for coverage datasets and reports. Elliot will own doc publication.

[02:29] Marcus Lin: That matches what I have.

[02:31] Kaitlyn Nguyen: Yep.

[02:34] Naomi Feldman: Great. Now timeline: We’re treating this as a two-quarter program, but we want customer-visible progress in weeks, not months.

[02:44] Naomi Feldman: Phase 1 is discovery plus inventory—2 to 3 weeks. Phase 2 is schema v1 plus shared libs—call it 3 to 5 weeks. Phase 3 instrumentation plus migration is the big one—6 to 10 weeks depending on how gnarly legacy stuff is. Phase 4 reliability plus reporting—3 to 6 weeks. Then beta/launch.

[03:12] Rafael Mendes: For reliability, I’d like to start earlier in parallel. Even if schema is not final, we can baseline current delivery lag.

[03:20] Naomi Feldman: Agree. But I think the “inventory first” approach is key to keep us from gold-plating schema and then discovering we missed half the actions.

[03:32] Mei Lin: +1. If we don’t inventory, we’ll just instrument whatever is easiest and then call it done.

[03:38] Marcus Lin: And from security, inventory drives threat model too. We can’t talk about bypass if we don’t know what we’re supposed to capture.

[03:47] Naomi Feldman: So decision #1: we start with a single master inventory of sensitive actions with mapping to expected audit events. Everyone aligned?

[03:57] (multiple): Yeah / yes.

[04:00] Naomi Feldman: Great. Mei, can you own the sheet and we’ll seed it across areas.

[04:05] Mei Lin: Yep, I’ll start with what we know: API keys, RBAC, org settings, model deploy/rollouts, dedicated scaling, private installer upgrades, data retention config, audit log config changes.

[04:18] Naomi Feldman: Perfect.

[04:20] Allison Grant: Quick question: are we deciding namespace conventions today? Because if we don’t, we’ll get a bunch of ad-hoc event names.

[04:29] Naomi Feldman: Let’s decide the direction and Allison can write the doc. I’m leaning towards namespaces by product surface: api.*, console.*, rbac.*, deploy.*, dedicated.*, private.*. And verbs like created/updated/deleted/rotated.

[04:47] Allison Grant: Works. I’ll draft naming guidelines and a reserved fields list.

[04:53] Marcus Lin: Please also include a rule like “no freeform event_name.” It should be registered.

[05:00] Nadia Rahman: Registry is good. Also helps validators.

[05:03] Naomi Feldman: Yep, we’ll include a registry + build-time check in the engineering plan.

[05:10] Kaitlyn Nguyen: On schema: can we talk required fields? Like, I need to know what I’m implementing for API key rotate.

[05:17] Naomi Feldman: Yes. Let’s list must-haves. I have: event_name, schema_version, timestamp, actor, target, org/workspace, request_id, ip, user_agent, outcome.

[05:33] Marcus Lin: And “actor” needs to model human user vs service identity. Because some changes are initiated by controllers.

[05:41] Nadia Rahman: + include “source” maybe? Like console vs API vs internal job.

[05:46] Allison Grant: That can be in actor or in metadata. But we should have a consistent field: maybe “actor.type” and “actor.display_name” and “actor.id”.

[05:57] Naomi Feldman: We have to remember JSON constraints from pipeline, but yes.

[06:02] Olga Petrov: Auditors also ask for “what changed.” Like the diff for RBAC. Not necessarily for every event, but for policy changes, yes.

[06:11] Kaitlyn Nguyen: That’s tricky because sometimes the payload includes secrets.

[06:15] Marcus Lin: Exactly. We need redaction rules: no tokens, no API key material, no passwords, no secrets. We can include before/after for role permissions, but not for any secret values.

[06:29] Naomi Feldman: Let’s capture as a principle: “include before/after where meaningful, but redact sensitive fields and never log secrets.”

[06:37] Rafael Mendes: Also, for “outcome” semantics: need success/failure and error codes. Because customers will ask “did the action fail.” And for us, if the audit event fails to deliver, that’s a problem.

[06:52] Nadia Rahman: Yeah. There are two “outcomes”: the business action outcome and the audit delivery outcome. The event should contain the business action outcome; delivery is measured via pipeline metrics.

[07:05] Naomi Feldman: Great point.

[07:08] Amara Diallo: On request_id: we currently have gateway request IDs, but I’m not sure they propagate to the internal services consistently, especially for console backend. Sometimes it gets renamed “reqId” or “x-request-id” and then dropped.

[07:23] Allison Grant: We should standardize field names, and a header name too.

[07:26] Naomi Feldman: So action item: Amara to map propagation, flag gaps.

[07:31] Amara Diallo: Yep.

[07:34] Naomi Feldman: Let’s talk about workstreams: Schema v1, library/validator, instrumentation slices, pipeline reliability/exporter.

[07:44] Nadia Rahman: For schema, I’d like to propose validation in two places: service-side validation to catch developer mistakes early, and pipeline validation as a backstop. But we need to watch latency overhead.

[07:58] Marcus Lin: I prefer pipeline validation as the enforcement point, because services can be bypassed or misconfigured.

[08:05] Nadia Rahman: I’m not saying only service. I’m saying both.

[08:09] Rafael Mendes: If pipeline rejects events, do we drop them? Or dead-letter queue? Because drop is unacceptable.

[08:16] Nadia Rahman: DLQ. And alert on schema validation failures.

[08:20] Naomi Feldman: Yes, DLQ plus alert. Also we should keep schema strict but allow forward-compat? Like unknown fields okay, but required fields must exist.

[08:34] Allison Grant: That’s classic JSONSchema approach: additionalProperties true, required fields enforced.

[08:40] Naomi Feldman: Great.

[08:42] Olga Petrov: Also retention guidance and redaction need to be written down. Customers will ask “how long do you retain IP addresses” and “can we export to SIEM.”

[08:52] Naomi Feldman: PRD will cover retention tiers and exports. Today we’re focusing on the backbone.

[08:58] Connor O'Brien: Just to timebox: 10 minutes left on schema and then 20 on milestones and action items.

[09:04] Naomi Feldman: Perfect.

[09:07] Kaitlyn Nguyen: For the inventory: do we define “sensitive action” by control area? Like auth, billing, deployment, retention. I can seed auth and RBAC.

[09:16] Naomi Feldman: Yes. Let’s do categories. Mei will create columns: action, system, owner, expected events, status.

[09:25] Mei Lin: I’ll do: subsystem, endpoint or UI action, event_name(s), actor type, target type, required fields check, test coverage.

[09:36] Marcus Lin: Add “risk if missing.” Helps prioritize.

[09:39] Mei Lin: Good call.

[09:42] Naomi Feldman: Instrumentation priorities: we want some early wins that are highly visible: API key create/rotate/revoke; RBAC role changes; and model rollout actions.

[09:57] Kaitlyn Nguyen: I can take API keys + RBAC. But for RBAC diffs, we need the source of truth for policy bundle. Jordan’s not here, but I can coordinate.

[10:07] Marcus Lin: For RBAC changes, the event must answer “who changed what,” ideally a normalized diff like added/removed permissions.

[10:16] Kaitlyn Nguyen: Yep.

[10:18] Naomi Feldman: For model rollouts, likely the runtime controllers and console both initiate changes. Actor attribution is critical.

[10:26] Nadia Rahman: Yeah, we’ll need to model “actor = service” with “impersonated_by” or “initiated_by” if it’s a controller acting on behalf of a user.

[10:37] Allison Grant: Careful: that becomes a nest of objects. But we can still model as string fields, like “actor_type=service”, “actor_id=runtime-controller”, “initiator_user_id=…”.

[10:49] Naomi Feldman: Let’s keep it simple for v1, but make sure it can represent both.

[10:55] Rafael Mendes: For delivery SLO: we need to define what “delivery” means. Persisted in audit store? Or exported to customer sink?

[11:04] Nadia Rahman: I think baseline SLO should be “persisted in primary audit log store.” Export is best-effort but with retries and metrics.

[11:13] Rafael Mendes: Agree. We can also have a secondary SLI for exporter lag.

[11:19] Olga Petrov: Auditors might care about immutability and tamper evidence. Is that in scope now?

[11:26] Marcus Lin: Threat model will cover that. But we can start with “append-only storage” and restricted access. If we do signing later, that’s roadmap.

[11:36] Naomi Feldman: Exactly. Not everything in v1. But we need to show “reasonable controls” now.

[11:44] Elliot Price: On docs: I can publish an “Audit logging program overview” page and link to schema draft, inventory sheet, and coverage dashboard once it exists.

[11:54] Naomi Feldman: Great.

[11:56] Naomi Feldman: Let’s jump to milestones. Connor, what do we need by end of week 1?

[12:02] Connor O'Brien: Week 1: start inventory sheet; draft naming guidelines; draft schema required fields; decide validation approach; create Linear initiative and workstreams.

[12:12] Naomi Feldman: Good.

[12:14] Connor O'Brien: Week 2: inventory v0 with top actions, assign owners; schema v1 draft with 2–3 example events; initial PR skeleton for schema validator (if engineering is ready).

[12:27] Naomi Feldman: Perfect. We’ll do a weekly sync until we hit beta.

[12:32] Naomi Feldman: Let’s open for questions.

[12:35] Amara Diallo: Question: do we consider console UI clicks as events even if they call the same API endpoint? Like should we log at the API layer only?

[12:44] Marcus Lin: Prefer logging at the source of truth where the action is executed—so the API/service layer. UI can be additional context but shouldn’t be the only place.

[12:54] Nadia Rahman: Exactly. If UI logs and API doesn’t, programmatic actions won’t be captured.

[12:59] Naomi Feldman: So: log where the change happens.

[13:02] Kaitlyn Nguyen: Another question: what about failed attempts? Like user tries to rotate key but is unauthorized. Do we log that?

[13:10] Marcus Lin: For sensitive actions, yes. Unauthorized attempts are themselves security relevant.

[13:16] Olga Petrov: And auditors like to see “failed attempts.”

[13:19] Naomi Feldman: Okay. So outcome includes failure and reason. Also we should ensure no PII beyond what’s needed.

[13:29] Allison Grant: “Reason” should be standardized error code, not a stack trace.

[13:34] Nadia Rahman: Right. error_code, maybe error_type, and a sanitized message.

[13:39] Rafael Mendes: And for SRE: ensure errors don’t blow cardinality. No freeform messages in metrics.

[13:46] Naomi Feldman: Great.

[13:48] Mei Lin: On coverage enforcement: are we expecting a CI check where adding a new “sensitive action” requires adding an event mapping? Or vice versa?

[13:56] Naomi Feldman: Both. The principle is: you can’t add a sensitive feature without registering the audit events and having tests. We’ll implement a coverage scanner that compares inventory vs emitted/validated event names.

[14:10] Marcus Lin: And exceptions require security sign-off.

[14:14] Naomi Feldman: Yes.

[14:16] Elliot Price: For the doc, should we call it “audit logging” or “audit logs” in headings? Minor but helps.

[14:21] Naomi Feldman: “Audit logs” in customer-facing, “audit logging” in engineering. But we can be consistent.

[14:28] Connor O'Brien: I’ll standardize in Linear.

[14:31] Naomi Feldman: Alright. I think we’ve got enough for today. Before we close, let’s read out action items so there’s no confusion.

[14:40] Naomi Feldman: Elliot: Confluence overview draft by Friday. Mei: inventory sheet seeded by Saturday-ish, top 30 actions. Allison: naming guideline draft by Thursday.

[14:54] Naomi Feldman: Kaitlyn: list of auth/RBAC + API key sensitive actions and expected events by Friday. Amara: request_id + actor propagation map by next Wednesday.

[15:08] Naomi Feldman: Nadia: recommendation for validation placement and perf concerns by next Tuesday. Rafael: baseline delivery lag numbers and SLO proposal by next Thursday.

[15:22] Naomi Feldman: Olga: SOC2/ISO evidence mapping outline by end of month. Marcus: redaction and security review checklist by next Tuesday.

[15:35] Naomi Feldman: Connor: two-quarter milestone plan and Linear initiative by Friday.

[15:42] (crosstalk) Sounds good / yep / okay.

[15:46] Marcus Lin: One more—please, everyone, remember: audit logs should not include secrets. If you’re unsure, ask. We will add tests to fail PRs if “token” shows up in payload.

[15:58] Kaitlyn Nguyen: Yeah, good. We’ve been burned by that.

[16:01] Naomi Feldman: Great. Thanks all. Next sync same time next week.

[16:07] Fireflies.ai: Meeting ended.

(Note: Transcript may be truncated due to recording start/stop timing; action items and decisions reflect the discussion as captured.)
